speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you please describe the location and character of your abdominal pain, and when did it start?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent heart attack and sudden onset of central abdominal pain with bloody stools, I am concerned about ischemic colitis or mesenteric ischemia. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of Abdomen and Pelvis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Angiography Abdomen Findings: Evidence suggestive of reduced blood flow to the mesenteric arteries.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT findings of reduced mesenteric blood flow, combined with your recent myocardial infarction and bloody stools, strongly suggest acute mesenteric ischemia. I will now request relevant medical images to further evaluate the extent of the bowel compromise. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of severe pain, bloody stools, and reduced mesenteric blood flow in a patient with recent MI is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Mesenteric Ischemia
